new_camps.name: Star Lake
new_camps.why: The base for Star Peak: the ridge starts from your tent, the descent returns to the same camp, and day three is a downhill carry out.
new_camps.notes: Camp at least 200 ft from the shore. Reach it by crossing Fish Creek Pass, dropping about a quarter mile and walking left. The only other option is a spot near the pass.

new_camps.name: Company Creek trailhead bivy
new_camps.why: Day one is short after the boat, so parties sleep near the trailhead and start the off-trail climb to the basin fresh the next day.
new_camps.notes: Night one is the least documented of the trip. The usual alternative, Bird Creek Camp on the Devore Creek Trail near 4,200 ft, is a different approach.

new_camps.name: High bivy in the larches southeast of Tupshin
new_camps.why: Flat spots in the highest larches put the east face a short walk away; parties sleep here before the climb and again after it.
new_camps.water: A creek runs near the site.
new_camps.capacity: A few flat spots about 200 ft above the basin floor.
new_camps.notes: Elevation is approximate. Reached after crossing the lower south ridge into the basin southeast of the peak; one party bivied at the base of the east cliff instead.

plan_conflict: Many parties reach Tupshin from Bird Creek Camp on the Devore Creek Trail; this plan's Company Creek and basin route has one documented trip.

new_camps.name: Swamp Creek camp on the PCT
new_camps.why: The end of an easy 8.5 miles on the PCT, with good water and flat ground before the steep off-trail climb the next morning.

new_camps.name: Upper Blue Basin camp
new_camps.why: The first flat ground after the brush, talus and slab climb from the creeks, splitting the carry before the final move up to the pass.
new_camps.notes: Off-trail, no maintained path; a camp below Asa Peak near 5,000 ft is the one reported.

new_camps.name: High camp near Icy-Spruce Pass
new_camps.why: The high camp for the south ridge: the long summit push starts and ends here, and you break camp from it on the way out.
new_camps.notes: Pass elevation is from the route description; other parties have camped on the Agnes Col.

camps.name: Dolomite Tower bivy caves
camps.why: Three flat platforms in shallow caves right of the start, one person each, so the 14 pitches begin at the base; spray blows in during wind and rain.

plan_conflict: Strong parties do the approach, climb and descent car-to-car in about 12.5 hours; the plan's second night at the caves exists only for a party that climbs slowly and sleeps again before the walk-off.

camps.name: Dolomite Camp
camps.why: At the top of the first step: the camp parties haul up and sleep at on the face, within reach of the upper steps.

camps.name: Couloir Camp
camps.why: A forested ledge about 1,000 ft above the lake that parties pass through; use it to split loads or sit out bad weather.

camps.name: Barclay Lake
camps.why: Comfortable lakeside sites at the foot of the approach; sleeping here adds the brush-bash to the start of a long day.

plan_conflict: The plan puts the bivy atop the crux step, but the documented camp on the face is Dolomite Camp at the top of the first step; Couloir Camp and Barclay Lake are changed from main to route.

new_camps.name: Camp near the Waptus River PCT bridge
new_camps.why: The usual camp for the Mega Slab climbs, about an hour from the slab base along the old Shovel Creek track; the summit day returns here.
new_camps.notes: One party camped on the abandoned trail beside Shovel Creek instead. Elevation not found in any source.

new_camps.name: Camp near the Waptus River PCT bridge
new_camps.why: The usual camp for the Mega Slab climbs, about an hour from the slab base along the old Shovel Creek track; the summit day returns here.
new_camps.notes: One party camped on the abandoned trail beside Shovel Creek instead. Elevation not found in any source.

new_camps.name: Dutch Miller Gap camp
new_camps.why: The standard camp after a long 15-mile walk-in: the face looms above, the summit day returns here, and ponds nearby give water.
new_camps.permit: Free self-issue wilderness permit at the trailhead.
new_camps.notes: Gap elevation is about 5,000 ft. Parties return here after the summit and hike out the next morning.

new_camps.name: Tarns below the Southwest Face, about 5,300 ft
new_camps.why: Moving up from the gap shortens the summit morning, at the cost of carrying packs another uphill mile past the gap.
new_camps.notes: Used by a 2020 party who moved camp from the gap the same evening.

camps.name: Chimney Glacier hanging basin — the big boulder bivy
camps.why: Puts the glacier about two hours away and has overhang space for a few bivy sacks; the summit day returns here before the hike out.

camps.name: Pete Lake and the Lemah Meadows camps
camps.why: An easy flat first night for late starters or a four-day trip, but it leaves a steep brushy climb to the bivy basin before the long summit day.

plan_conflict: Fit parties return to the bivy and hike out the same evening, so night 2 is only spent there on the three-day plan.

camps.name: Chimney Glacier hanging basin — the big boulder bivy
camps.why: The standard high camp below the glacier toe, with a sheltered overhang; summit day starts and ends here before the hike out.

camps.name: Sunrise Knob
camps.why: Mapped at about 4,650 ft in the same basin; an alternative bench when the boulder bivy is taken by another party.

camps.name: Pete Lake and the Lemah Meadows camps
camps.why: A flat, easy night for parties that start late, but it adds a steep brushy climb to the high camp and lengthens summit day.

plan_conflict: Both the boulder bivy and Sunrise Knob are on file as main; Sunrise Knob is changed to route.

camps.name: Chimney Glacier hanging basin — the big boulder bivy
camps.why: The usual high camp below the glacier toe, with sheltered bivy space under the boulder; summit day starts and ends a short moraine walk away.

camps.name: Sunrise Knob
camps.why: Mapped at about 4,650 ft in the same basin; an alternative when the boulder bivy is occupied, with the same short approach to the glacier.

camps.name: Pete Lake and the Lemah Meadows camps
camps.why: An easy flat first night with plenty of space, but it leaves the steep brushy climb to the glacier basin for the morning of the summit day.

plan_conflict: Both the boulder bivy and Sunrise Knob are on file as main; Sunrise Knob is changed to route.

camps.name: Pete Lake and the Lemah Meadows camps
camps.why: Easy flat miles to sites by Pete Lake or along Lemah Creek; the creek-side sites save about three miles on summit day over staying at the lake.

camps.name: Williams Lake and the upper Middle Fork meadows below Dutch Miller Gap
camps.why: The first real camp up the valley, only a short climb from the gap and the peak; lake and meadow sites give water and room, and summit day returns here.

camps.name: Hardscrabble Horse Camp, Middle Fork Snoqualmie
camps.why: Staging camp at the end of the closed road; sleeping here shortens day one but adds about seven trail miles to the summit day.

camps.name: Waptus Lake, with Spade Lake above it
camps.why: The gentle eastern approach from Salmon la Sac; a pleasant first night but it adds a long climb to the gap before the peak.

camps.name: Summit Chief Valley gravel flats
camps.why: A flat gravel wash directly below the face, a short way off the trail; the climb and the descent both start and end at your tent.

camps.name: Hardscrabble Horse Camp, Middle Fork Snoqualmie
camps.why: A lower option at the road end; it spares the cross-country day with a heavy pack but adds miles and gain to summit day.

camps.name: Peggy's Pond, below Cathedral Rock
camps.why: The pond is where this loop ends, not where it sleeps: you pass it on summit day on the way down to the trailhead.

camps.name: Hyas Lake and Upper Hyas Lake
camps.why: An easy low camp close to the trailhead for a three-day trip; it adds a long climb to Deception Pass and the lakes before the glacier.

new_camps.name: Pea Soup Lake outlet
new_camps.why: The usual camp for the Lynch Glacier: the glacier is minutes away, and summit day skips the long climb up from Jade Lake.
new_camps.notes: Elevation is approximate. Lies over Dip Top Gap from Jade Lake; be ready to camp on snow early in the season.

new_camps.name: Jade Lake
new_camps.why: A lower, more sheltered camp reached without crossing the gap; it adds the steep Dip Top Gap snow climb to the morning of summit day.
new_camps.notes: Elevation is the plan's figure for the lake.

plan_conflict: The plan names Jade Lake first, but the documented party slept at the Pea Soup Lake outlet; Pea Soup is made main and Jade route.

camps.name: La Bohn Lakes, La Bohn Gap and the Chain Lakes benches
camps.why: Camps right under the gap, so summit day is a short scramble and returns to the tent; the price is a longer, steeper first day with a snow slope to the gap.

camps.name: Necklace Valley — Jade, Emerald and Opal Lakes
camps.why: Established lake sites eight to nine miles in, lower and buggier; stopping here keeps day one easier but adds the gap climb to summit day.

camps.name: Money Creek and Miller River campgrounds, Foss River roadhead
camps.why: Car campgrounds for the night before an early trailhead start; useful for a Friday-night arrival, though the Foss River road has had delays.

plan_conflict: Both La Bohn Lakes and Necklace Valley are on file as main; Necklace Valley is changed to route.

new_camps.name: Jade Lake, Necklace Valley
new_camps.why: Established sites at the end of the nine-mile first day; the summit day over La Bohn Gap returns here, and Emerald and Opal give quieter sites.
new_camps.permit: A wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead at no fee.
new_camps.notes: Buggy early in the season; campfires are not allowed. Some parties move up to La Bohn Lakes for night 2.

camps.name: Rock benches above Overcoat Glacier
camps.why: The highest camp, at the base of the summit snow; it makes summit day short but means a hard, brushy carry up from the valley.

camps.name: Overcoat Lake
camps.why: A lower base reached after the same brush, with water; it saves some of the carry but adds climbing to summit day.

camps.name: Hardscrabble Horse Camp, Middle Fork Snoqualmie
camps.why: The end of the bike ride and the last night before the car; it keeps the loaded carry short but makes day one a long ride and walk.

plan_conflict: The plan's night 2 near Bears Breast Tarns could not be confirmed in any source, and Overcoat Lake is changed from main to route.
Parties camp on the valley floor below the face (one trip climbed from camp and returned to it), but no source gives the camp's elevation.
